If the same surface is illuminated with light of wavelength $2\lambda$, the stopping potential is ${V}_{0}$. The threshold wavelength for this surface for the photoelectric effect is
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation

$e{V}_{s} = E - ϕ$

${V}_{s} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambdae} - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{0}e}$

$3{V}_{0} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambdae} - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{0}e}$...(i)

${V}_{0} = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambdae} - \dfrac{hc}{{\lambda}_{0}e}$...(ii)

$0 = - \dfrac{hc}{2\lambdae} + \dfrac{2hc}{{\lambda}_{0}e}$

${\lambda}_{0} = 4\lambda$

questions.q: Light of two different frequencies whose photons have energies $1$ eV and $2.5$ eV, respectively, successively illuminate a metallic surface whose work function is $0.5$ eV. The ratio of maximum speeds of the emitted electrons will be
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is ${K}_\max = hυ - {ϕ}_{0}$

Where $hυ$ is the energy of incident photon and ${ϕ}_{0}$ is the work function.

But ${K}_\max = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_\max^{2}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_\max^{2} = hυ - {ϕ}_{0}$

As per question,

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\max_{1} ⁡ = 1eV - \text{0.5}eV = \text{0.5}eV$ ...(i)

and $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\max_{2} ⁡ = \text{2.5}eV - \text{0.5}eV = 2eV$ ...(ii)

Dividing equation (i) by equation (ii), we get

$\dfrac{v^{2}\max_{1} ⁡}{v^{2}\max_{2} ⁡} = \dfrac{\text{0.5}eV}{2eV} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{{v}_{\max_{1} ⁡}}{{v}_{\max_{2} ⁡}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.solution:
The acceleration of the electron is

$a = \dfrac{eE}{m}$

The velocity of the electron as a function of time is

$v = at = \dfrac{eE}{m}t$

The de-Broglie wavelength is

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m\left(\dfrac{eE}{m}\right)t}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{eEt}$
$\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt} = - \dfrac{h}{eEt^{2}}$

Eienstein's photoelectric equation is given as,
